Isn't the fun of a game the "journey"?

For a lot of people, the fun of a game is the challenge, the ability to set themselves to a difficult task and succeed. During normal gameplay, that task is simply to win the game.

Once a player figures out how to do that, though, the challenge of the game goes away, in most cases. So, in order to keep the game interesting for a longer period of time, many players will set themselves special self-imposed challenges that make the game more difficult.

They might prohibit themselves from using certain items, or force themselves to completely avoid using certain game mechanics that would give them an advantage.

A speedrun is one such kind of challenge, where their difficult task is simply to win the game as fast as possible. More specifically, they may be trying to outpace their last playthrough, or they may be trying to outpace the world record speed.

In every case I've ever seen, the speedrunner was a player who had already completed the game normally multiple times, and now wanted to make it more interesting by adding a new challenge to it. Since there is already a large speedrunner community, and a speedrun is usually an easy challenge to set up, speedrunning is usually the first choice of such a player.

Does that make any sense?
